### Summary

The boundary chapter derives the identities exercised by the report checks. No extra numerical scheme is
introduced here. A source assertion is evidence of intended coverage, not evidence that a pinned build passed.
All solver entries below refer to `e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0`, except the row marked "main after chengcli/snapy#303", which refers to `9ad0936779ae001dba65c9eafccaa7c058686c97`. Their numerical thresholds are test constants, not measured results.

Separate source-defined solver assertions from executed report checks.
No solver tests run for this chapter; seven report formula checks are available.
Default: catalogue only, no solver configuration change.
Pins: one test row describes main at snapy@9ad0936779ae001dba65c9eafccaa7c058686c97 (chengcli/snapy#303); the rest is at snapy@e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0.

### Derivation

### Numerical method

Run report checks without a compiled solver. For new solver evidence, first configure a CPU-only build at the
pin and resolve the pinned dependencies. Record the complete command, deck, dtype, ranks and environment.
Run a focused boundary filter before expanding coverage. CUDA and multi-process assertions remain separate
claims and are not inferred from a CPU formula check.

The all-face mode suite is device-parameterized; the explicit CPU/CUDA comparison skips when CUDA is
unavailable. The panel and wall-reference suites have explicit CPU and conditional CUDA arms. Saturation
instantiates CPU and CUDA when built with CUDA. Rectification chooses CUDA when the test helper enables it;
the flip-count test is explicitly a CPU one-thread/eight-thread comparison. The Python solid runner exposes
a device in its result, so the actual run must record that choice. A local multi-block panel assertion does
not imply more than one process; the exchange registration separately requests two processes.

The outline's positivity suites remain an inventory here: their detailed flux budgets belong to the positivity
chapter. The source registration links above identify the dry and moist panel variants without claiming they
passed. The pulse comparison does not assert the extrapolation arm. The two-grid reference threshold does
not satisfy the three-resolution rule for a newly measured report order.

The report checks are `src/snapy_report/ch11/boundary_check.py`, with committed output
`src/snapy_report/ch11/boundary_check.out`. They check C1 copy/parity/corner ownership, C2 acoustic inversion,
C3 shared admissibility, C4 corner averaging, C5 DP optimality against exhaustive enumeration, C6 block closure,
and C7 reference moments/continuation. C5 covers 508 binary inputs; all checks use exact symbolic or rational
identities, so their expected residual is exactly zero. These numbers are produced by that script, not snapy.

### Limits

No compiled CPU, CUDA or multi-rank solver test has run for this chapter. The only status shown for the row marked
"main after chengcli/snapy#303" is the suite count in the body of that PR, not a run of that test at
snapy@9ad0936779ae001dba65c9eafccaa7c058686c97; at snapy@e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0 the
gnomonic-equiangle block of `curved_energy` is not checked for $E+P$. Runtime sound-speed/EOS behaviour,
nonorthogonal momentum conversion, outflow with VIC/WB, thin solid geometries, scalar/diffusion solid coupling,
and stretched-grid wall convergence remain missing evidence. A future measured wall-order claim needs at least
three resolutions at the pin. The complete configuration inventory is @sec-ch12-matrix.
